name: Weekly burst-firing, both temporal lobes, 30 min (Baker-Price & Persinger)
origin: Baker-Price & Persinger, Persinger/Koren lab, Laurentian University
summary: The bilateral-temporal arm of Baker-Price & Persinger's open-label studies of depression after closed head injury: 30 min of 1 uT burst-firing fields through both temporal lobes, once a week for 5 weeks (1996, 4 patients) or 6 weeks (2003, 7 of 14 patients). The authors reported lower depression scores, but there was no sham arm and the left-frontal arm improved as much.
notes: In 1996 four patients got a 'complex, burst-firing magnetic field (1 microT)' through the temporoparietal regions from two 10-cm by 7-cm boxes of four solenoids each, 'once every 4 sec.', 30 min a week for 5 weeks (Baker-Price 1996 p.4 [494]). In 2003, 7 of 14 patients got it for 6 weeks, 'once every 3 sec.', one pair (one solenoid in each box) on at a time for 0.5 s (Baker-Price 2003 p.4 [968]). This program follows 1996: a 690-ms burst (230 points of 3 ms), then a 4-s pause. The lab uses 'once every 4 s' for the pause between bursts (Persinger 1999 p.3 [165]). The 2003 paper prints 259 values; the 230 here follow Persinger 2000. The burst is rebuilt as this project's rising sweep with the published point duration and length; the point values were never published as numbers, only as a small graph (Persinger 2000 Fig. 2, p.5 [663]). One left-right pair is on at a time (0.5 s each), and the right side is reversed so that the pair's field points through the head. The four sites per side stand for the four solenoids of each box (in the lab helmet, an ellipse of 7.5 by 5 cm); the site names are this project's reading. Field: 1 uT; where it was measured is not stated. This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. No sham arm, 4 and 14 patients, never repeated outside the lab. Rats given the same weekly field spent about half as much time in the open arms of a plus maze after two sessions (Fitzpatrick & Persinger 2004 p.1). Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). This was clinical research on diagnosed patients, not a treatment: depression and head injury need a clinician. A head injury raises seizure risk. Not for anyone with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on headache, nausea or distress.
setting: Seated or reclined, eyes closed, in a quiet room. The studies were an outpatient clinical series with depression questionnaires before and after (and QEEG in 2003).
schedule: 30 min once a week for 5 weeks (1996) or 6 weeks (2003), followed in 2003 by 6 weeks without sessions.
